title: Merging Ion Concentration Polarization between Juxtaposed Ion Exchange Membranes to Block the Propagation of the Polarization Zone
protocol: Design two kinds of silicon masters using conventional photolithography or deep reactive ion etching.
Silanize the micropatterned silicon masters with trichlorosilane for 30 minutes in a vacuum jar.
Mix a silicone elastomer base with a curing agent at a ratio of 10:1 and place the mixture in a vacuum jar to remove bubbles.
Pour uncured PDMS on the silicon masters, remove any remaining bubbles with a blower, and cure the PDMS at 80 °C for 2 hours in a convection oven.
Detach the cured PDMS from the silicon masters.
Shape the detached PDMS properly using a knife to form squared shapes.
Cut half of the PDMS mold perpendicularly to the two parallel microchannels.
Punch holes at the ends of the PDMS channels with a 2.0-mm biopsy punch.
Clean a glass slide and the PDMS mold with tape and a blower.
Attach the PDMS mold onto the glass slide for reversible attachment.
Release approximately 10 µL of cation exchange resin at the open end of the sliced channel.
Place the syringe head on the punched holes.
Pull the plunger to create a gentle negative pressure.
Pull the cation exchange resin into the two channels.
Detach the PDMS mold without touching the patterned resin.
Place the glass slide on the heater at 95 °C for 5 min to evaporate the solvent in the resin.
Peel off the unnecessary part of the patterned membrane with a razor blade, making two separated line-patterns.
Punch two holes at the ends of microchannels and another two holes where the membrane patterns will be located after bonding the PDMS channel to the membrane-patterned substrate.
Bond the PDMS microchannel to the membrane-patterned substrate immediately after oxygen plasma treatment for 40 s at 100 W and 50 mTorr.

Prepare various test solutions including 1-100 mM KCl, 1 mM NaCl (pH ~7), the mixture of 1 mM NaCl and 0.2 mM HCl (pH ~3.7), the mixture of 1 mM NaCl and 0.2 mM NaOH (pH ~10.3), and 1x phosphate-buffered saline.
Add a negatively charged fluorescent dye (~1.55 µM) to the test solutions.
Load the sample solution in one reservoir of the channel and apply negative pressure to the other reservoir to fill the channel with the solution.
Connect the two reservoirs hydrodynamically by releasing a large droplet to eliminate the pressure gradient along the channel.
Fill the two reservoirs, which are connected to the cation exchange patterns, with buffer solutions (1 M KCl or 1 M NaCl) using a syringe or pipet.
Place wires at the reservoirs across the two patterned membranes (anode on the left reservoir and cathode on the right).
Connect the wires with a source measurement unit.
Load the ICP device onto an inverted epifluorescence microscope.
Apply a voltage (0.5-100 V) and measure the current response with a source measurement unit.
Capture fluorescent images using a charge-coupled device camera.
Analyze the fluorescent intensity using imaging software.
